recommendation.summary: dsh-tui 0.11.2 is an interactive terminal UI plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Author intent is a single TUI plane installed as the named profile `dsh-tui` (`dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`, then `dsh-tui` == `dsh --profile dsh-tui`). Node: README states CI uses Node 24 and the package supports `^22.19 || >=24`; engines.node in both source and published manifests is `^22.19 || >=24`. Preferred major is 24 (CI-configured and README-stated); 22 is a declared-support baseline from the engines range, not an author preference. Development package manager is pnpm 11.21.0 (packageManager field); the documented consumer install path uses global npm with no pinned version. The one evidenced author DSH baseline is 0.2.0-rc.1, named in README as the primary compatibility target and pinned as the primary validated line in the pnpm-workspace dev tree. No headless/SDK/ACP workflow is documented, so only tui is selected. Note the Radar target 0.2.0-rc.2 is not covered by the plugin's peer ranges (they end at 0.2.0-rc.1); this is an unverified-compatibility gap, not a proven incompatibility. No plugin-documented disabled/offline startup flags were evidenced.

conclusion.statement: dsh-tui 0.11.2 (@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui) was reviewed and exercised on the single author-intended TUI plane. Review: author intent is the named profile `dsh-tui` (`dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`, then `dsh-tui` == `dsh --profile dsh-tui`); preferred Node major 24 (README states CI uses Node 24; engines.node `^22.19 || >=24` in source and published manifests), with 22 as a declared-support baseline; development package manager pnpm 11.21.0; the one evidenced author DSH baseline is 0.2.0-rc.1. Launch f9d49183b72c4d8b82e681b6c4911a34 finished with exitCode 0, 8 executed cells (4 native, 4 surface, 0 adapter), 0 failed tasks, 0 deferred. Native plane: on the author baseline DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 the exact artifact installed, registered, loaded and satisfied its direct Node peer contracts on both Node 22 (dsh-tui-node22-dsh-e221349d43ed) and Node 24 (dsh-tui-node24-dsh-e221349d43ed) -> compatible. On the Radar target DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 both native cells (dsh-tui-node22, dsh-tui-node24) are install-failed: the traced DSH plugin install command failed, consistent with the plugin's peer ranges ending at 0.2.0-rc.1. TUI surface plane: on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 the profile was created by `dsh plugin add`, install/registration/host/surface/interaction all passed and the TUI produced a frame on both Node 22 (dsh-tui-node22-tui-dsh-fccc17ae9a5c) and Node 24 (dsh-tui-node24-tui-dsh-28c6855f163b), but both are surface-incompatible because the TUI produced a frame and did not stop after the bounded shutdown input (shutdown stage failed). On DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 the two TUI cells (dsh-tui-node22-tui, dsh-tui-node24-tui) are unknown: the profile install timed out at 180 s while pnpm was still resolving/downloading (532 packages added, minimumReleaseAgeExclude rewritten), so no bounded result exists; this is an install-timeout observation, not a proven plugin defect. No SDK/ACP plane was selected or exercised (adapterCells 0). accepted/compatible here means the report was recorded and the native contract checks passed on rc.1; it does not establish consumer compatibility, and the rc.2 install failures plus the rc.1 TUI shutdown failure are recorded as observed, not as proven incompatibility of the plugin's own code.
coverageNotes: Radar target DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 is outside the plugin's declared peer ranges (they end at 0.2.0-rc.1); both rc.2 native cells failed at the traced plugin install step and both rc.2 TUI cells timed out during profile install, so rc.2 compatibility is unverified.

The TUI shutdown stage failed on the author baseline DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 on both Node 22 and Node 24: a frame was produced but the process did not stop after the bounded shutdown input. Recorded as surface-incompatible for the bounded check; the cause was not diagnosed further.

The two DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 TUI cells are unknown rather than failed: the profile install hit the 180 s bound while pnpm was still resolving and downloading, so no bounded install/registration/surface result exists.
No SDK or ACP plane was selected or exercised (adapterCells 0); the plugin documents only the interactive TUI workflow.

Windows-specific defaults (danger-full-access sandbox, approval never) and the win32 input-record path were not exercised.
Migration subcommands (dsh-tui migrate) and the VS Code / Herdr integrations were not exercised.
